title: Cookie Oatmeal Sandwich with Peanut Butter and Jelly Filling

content.title: About
content.content: The cookie oatmeal sandwich with peanut butter and jelly filling consists of two soft oatmeal cookie layers bound together by a sweet, creamy filling. It combines the crunchy texture of oat, the rich taste of peanut butter, and the fruity sweetness of jelly.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Oats are rich in beta‑glucan, which supports heart health.
Peanut butter contains more monounsaturated fats than many other nut spreads.
Jelly is often made from berries high in antioxidants such as blueberry or strawberry.
Cookie sandwiches are popular in school lunches and as quick snacks.
The combination of oats, peanut butter, and jelly provides a balanced mix of carbs, protein, and healthy fats.

items.title: Energy Support
items.content: Complex carbohydrates from oats and quick sugars from jelly give both sustained and rapid energy.

items.title: High in Fiber
items.content: Oats provide soluble and insoluble fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Beneficial Fats
items.content: Peanut butter supplies monounsaturated fats that support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Vitamins and Minerals
items.content: Berry jelly adds vitamin C and antioxidants, while peanut butter contributes vitamin E, magnesium, and phosphorus.

items.title: Satiety
items.content: The mix of protein, fat, and fiber helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Peanut Allergy
items.content: Peanut butter can trigger severe allergic reactions in individuals with peanut allergy.

items.title: High Sugar Content
items.content: Jelly often contains added sugar, which may be a concern for blood‑glucose management.

items.title: Caloric Density
items.content: The sandwich is calorie‑dense due to fats in peanut butter and sugar in jelly; portion control is advised.

items.title: Oxalate Content
items.content: Oats and peanuts contain oxalates, which in excess can contribute to kidney stone formation.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy the sandwich as a standalone snack, cut into bite‑size pieces for kids, or pack it in lunch boxes. A brief microwave warm‑up can make the filling softer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in an airtight container in a cool, dry place. For longer shelf life, store in the refrigerator to prevent the peanut butter from going rancid. Discard if it develops a moldy smell or off‑flavor.
